blocks.text: 以简洁实现智能体互操作性

inlines.text: 以简洁实现智能体互操作性

blocks.text: 一个 skill 是一个包含 SKILL.md 文件的文件夹，用于教会智能体执行特定任务或领域知识，以及它所需的任何脚本或参考资料。我们在开发 Claude Code 时开发了 skills。它能很好地处理一般知识工作，但往往缺乏真实业务任务所需的程序性知识。在我们 2025 年 10 月发布后的几周内，开发者在 GitHub 上发布了数千个 skills，并为 Codex、Cursor 和 OpenCode 编写了加载器。随后，我们将 Agent Skills 作为开放标准发布，拥有独立的 GitHub 组织和域名，以便任何智能体都可以使用它。到目前为止，已发布 100 万个 skills，安装量接近 2.8 亿次。

blocks.text: 将 Agent Skills 捐赠给 AAIF

inlines.text: 将 Agent Skills 捐赠给 AAIF

blocks.text: 我们致力于保持 Agent Skills 开放、社区驱动和供应商中立。今天，我们将该标准捐赠给 Linux 基金会下的 Agentic AI Foundation（AAIF），该基金会由我们与 Block 和 OpenAI 于去年共同创立，我们此前已向其捐赠了 Model Context Protocol（MCP）。AAIF 将作为该标准未来的中立家园，确保社区在 Agent Skills 的未来方向上拥有发言权。

blocks.text: Today, we’re donating Agent Skills, the open standard that gives AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows, to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). More than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code, have integrated Agent Skills since we published the standard in December 2025.

blocks.text: Agent interoperability through simplicity

inlines.text: Agent interoperability through simplicity

blocks.text: A skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file that teaches an agent a specific task or domain, along with any scripts or reference material it needs. We developed skills while working on Claude Code. It handled general knowledge work well, but often lacked the procedural knowledge that real business tasks need. Within weeks of our October 2025 launch, developers published thousands of skills on GitHub and wrote loaders for Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode. We then published Agent Skills as an open standard, under its own GitHub organization and domain, so any agent could use it. So far, 1 million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed.

blocks.text: Donating Agent Skills to AAIF

inlines.text: Donating Agent Skills to AAIF

blocks.text: We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community-driven, and vendor-neutral. Today, we are donating the standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, which we co-founded with Block and OpenAI last year, and to which we donated the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The AAIF will provide a neutral home to the standard going forward, ensuring the community has a say in where Agent Skills go next.

blocks.text: What comes next

inlines.text: What comes next

blocks.text: We’ve proposed starting with a roadmap covering versioned releases, a formal proposal process, and security guidance for people who write and install skills. As with MCP, the project will continue to prioritize community input and transparent decision-making. You can join the project’s Discord to give feedback on proposed specification changes.
